narrative: Demand for PL1__MC9C6CAA is smooth (CV=0.209) with no significant trend over the 216-day observation window, though 6 extreme low-demand days were winsorized. Lead times are highly volatile (CV=0.667), contributing 93.3% of total lead-time demand variance and making lead-time variability the primary driver of safety stock requirements. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy was selected to provide a precise reorder trigger that responds directly to inventory position, matching the smooth daily demand profile and volatile lead-time environment. The recommended safety stock of 3,503 units replaces the current SAP zero-buffer, achieving 95% service level while keeping total inventory within the 13,956-unit storage cap.
warnings: SAP safety stock is currently 0; stockout risk is high without safety stock.
Lead time CV=0.667 is high; supplier reliability improvement recommended.
6 demand outliers (extreme low values) were winsorized at 1st/99th percentile.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand (CV=0.209) with volatile lead times (CV=0.667) favours a continuous-review model. The (r,Q) policy immediately triggers a fixed replenishment order when inventory falls to the reorder point, providing precise stockout protection against lead-time uncertainty without the overhead of a periodic-review system.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 13,956 units reduces maximum order quantity headroom to 10,453 units above safety stock. With EOQ of 8,149 and SS of 3,503, combined maximum inventory is 11,652 units (83.5% utilisation) — the cap does not currently bind but leaves limited buffer for demand spikes or expedited orders.
